- Official press release: https://www.admin.ch/de/newnsb/UA8hylpLYO6i ( Bundesamt news) or https://www.bfs.admin.ch/bfs/de/home/statistiken/preise/landesindex-konsumentenpreise.html (topic page — mentions 101.7) or statistik.admin.ch/de/news/2026-0059. e-fundresearch: Next publication Nov... Dec 2.
- lik-app.bfs.admin.ch/de/lik/rechner: 12.2020=100 basis: 10.2025 = 107.2, 10.2026 = 108.7. Nov 2025 in 12.2020=100 =? For YoY 1.6% in Nov 2026 need Nov 2025 index in same base. From lik-app maybe; or from the e-fundresearch/BFS.

For phase-1, the live calculator for ch-cpi can parse the BFS/statistik.admin.ch press page: Oct 2026 101.7 (Dec 2025=100), +1.5% YoY, +0.2% MoM. For the "Nov ≥ 1.6%" market: YoY Nov 2026 ≥ 1.6% requires Nov 2026 index ≥ 1.016 × Nov 2025 index. Need Nov 2025 index: With Dec 2025=100 base, Nov 2025 < 100 (Nov 2025 = 99.x?). From press release Nov 2025 (published Dec 2025, old base 2020=100): "Nov 2025: -0.2% MoM, +0.1% YoY" or similar. We could fetch the Nov 2025 BFS press release. Search result refbase: https://www.admin.ch/de/newnsb/... For time, in the live refresher I'll fetch a BFS press-release page that states both. The lik-app seems to hold a full series (Startwert/Endwert calculator = JS app with data? the search snippet shows: Startdatum 10.2025 Startwert 107.2 Punkte Enddatum 10.2026 Endwert 108.7). The lik-app might expose a JSON API. Let me test lik-app schemas.

Actually — let me pause the deep data hunting. The scale of this task: I've been asked to implement ALL 21 fixes. The core is the live miner with per-topic refreshers. I've now got verified replacement URLs for the 5 dead sources:

1. **Destatis**: https://www.destatis.de/DE/Presse/Pressemitteilungen/2026/11/PD26_392_611.html (200, verified, "Verbraucherpreisindex, Oktober 2026: +2,8 %... Indexstand 126,5" via Gesamtindex table). Nov 2025 series: PD25_447_611.html (122,7). Both verified 200.
2. **BK postal-voting**: stadt-zuerich.ch stimmbeteiligung page (200, live 39.6%) + gfsbern 2nd SRG survey for participation intention. QA said "BK admin postal-voting page" — bk.admin.ch has no live return-rate page in this world; the live equivalent is the City of Zurich "Stand Stimmbeteiligung" page. I'll use that + gfsbern.
3. **SRG Wählbarometer**: https://www.gfsbern.ch/de/news/2-srg-trendumfrage-zur-eidg-abstimmung-vom-29-november-2026/ (200, verified: KM 49/46, Teilnahmeabsicht 52%).
4. **Electografía**: https://www.electografica.com/2026/11/encuesta-data10-261123.html (200, verified: VOX 19.1%, 64 seats).
5. **FIDE match page**: https://www.fide.com/new-documents/ (200, verified: "FACT SHEET – Game 2 ... Match score: 1–1" + color allocation for game 3).

Also supporting live URLs:
- Wikipedia siteinfo API (200): articles 7,269,403.
- GitHub milestones API (200): Go1.27.5 = #457, open 14 / closed 18.
- oven-sh/bun releases (200): bun-v1.4.5 2026-11-19.

- Datatracker ballot (200): draft-ietf-mpls-mna-ioam-18, IESG Evaluation... need detail for ballot state. Let me fetch its content + the Datatracker JSON API.
- go.dev/doc/devel/release (200) — minors were only the majors in my grep; check format for go1.27.x listings.
- BFS Lik news: https://www.admin.ch/de/newnsb/UA8hylpLYO6i or bfs topic page (200).

Remaining to verify: Datatracker ballot content, go.dev minors listing, lik-app or BFS Nov 2025 index (for the ch-cpi calculator), Bun untagged commits (maybe skip — recompute from release gaps only), FIDE color allocation for game 8 (hard — schedule says games on certain dates; colors alternate; the FACT SHEET says G3 Sindarov White "for the second time" → G1 Sindarov White, G2 Gukesh White, G3 Sindarov White... pattern: Sindarov White in odd games? Then Game 8 → Gukesh White (Sindarov Black). Hmm — wait, alternate games: In recent WCCs, players alternate colors every game in the first stretch then swap... Actually since 2021 rules: colors drawn for game 1 and then alternate each game? 2023: Gukesh White in games 2,3?? No.

The official Fide WCC 2026: 14 games. "Javokhir Sindarov will have the white pieces for the second time in the match tomorrow (game three)" → Sindarov White in G1 and G3. So alternation: G1: Sindarov W; G2: Gukesh W; G3: Sindarov W; ... G8: Gukesh W? If it's strict odd/even alternation: odd games Sindarov White, even games Gukesh White. Game 8 = even → Gukesh White, Sindarov Black. So "Sindarov strictly more points after game 8"... The market rail: "After Game 8 (Dec 3, 2026), will Sindarov have strictly more points than Gukesh". Wait the schedule said Game 7 Dec 2, Game 8 Dec 3? The chess.com games list: "Game 3 - Nov 26, Game 4 - Nov 28, Game 5 - Nov 29, Game 6 - Nov 30, Game 7 - Dec 2..." so Game 8 - Dec 3. Market cutoff Dec 2 13:00 UTC — fine.

Sindarov performance vs Gukesh: Gukesh is rated 2710 vs Sindarov 2782 (Sindarov the higher-rated!). The fixture math used "Sindarov White vs 2750+: 30/55/15". For live, compute from live rating + base rates. Given match score 1-1 after 2 games (both draws).

Market price 63.2% yes... wait which way? market address 0x42fd yes 0.631773 — the question "will Sindarov have strictly more points than Gukesh after game 8" is presumably the YES at 63%?? That seems high given a 1-1 tie. Hmm, actually no — since the market asks about "Sindarov strictly more" and it's priced 63%, the market must believe Sindarov (2782) will outperform. Our evidence: 1-1 after 2 games, Sindarov has 2750+ rating edge... P(YES) estimate: Sindarov will have strictly more points after G8. From 1-1, over 6 games with advantage ~+0.2/game... hard. Our evidence rating: maybe slightly lower than market. derived P(yes) needs to be computed via some method from live data (ratings, current score). The markov_lead calculator handles "leader points" — but now there's no leader (tie). Analysis kind 'markov_lead' requires leaderPoints != trailerPoints. For a tie, need a different computation. Live refresher could compute expected points via ratings → probability of lead after 6 more games via normal approximation.

This is where I should keep the recompute honest and simple: compute P(Sindarov leads after 6 more games | tie now) using per-game win/draw/loss probabilities derived from live rating gap (2782 vs 2710, Δ=72 Elo): expected score s = 1/(1+10^(-72/400)) ≈ 0.599. Then model per game (White avg vs Black avg ~ 55/35/10 typical conditions...) — I need an assumption from live data... the only live-observable base rates: the two games drew. I could use Elo-diff → expected score, plus observed draw tendency at the top (both games drawn). Simple approach: simulate 6 games with win prob w, draw d derived from Elo + observed draws: e.g., expected points/game μ = 0.599, split between wins and draws... but draw rate q must be assumed. Better to use the Python calculator with a "match_lead_from_tie" analysis: inputs: games remaining, expected score per game from Elo, assumed draw share from observed... The zero-hallucination rule applies to numbers in the note, not to statistical assumptions (they can be modeled and stated as model assumptions).

OK — rather than perfect per-market modeling, the architecture counts: live refreshers extract live numbers, recompute analysis params, and mark assumptions clearly. For fide-game8, the model: expected score = 1/(1+10^(-ΔElo/400)); assume draw probability = observed draw rate among classical WCC games at similar level (say from live stats? too deep) — I'll parameterize with the two observed draws fact: drawRate = 2/2 observed with huge uncertainty, plus historical... I'll state assumption "draw share 60% of decided-score" — hmm. Simplest defensible: per-game points distribution: P(win)=x, P(draw)=y, P(loss)=z with x+z... Let me just do: expected score margin per game μ = s - 0.5 (s = Elo expected). Define draw share d (model assumption, e.g. d=0.55 observed at top level), then P(win) = (μ + d/2)... Actually given expected score s = x + y/2, and x + y + z = 1: set y = d (draw share assumption), then x - z = 2s - 1 = 0.198; x = (1 - d + 0.198)/2, z = (1 - d - 0.198)/2. With d = 0.85 (top-level match draws)... x = (0.15+0.198)/2 = 0.174, z = (0.15-0.198)/2 = -0.024 → negative, so d must be < 0.802. Use d=0.7: x=0.249, z=0.051. Hmm the draw share assumption matters a lot. Alternative cleaner: directly estimate probability that Sindarov leads after 6 games given per-expected-margin ~0.099/game × 6 = 0.594 points expected lead, sd from game-level variance σ_game ≈ sqrt of points variance (~0.35)... P(lead>0) via normal: mean 0.594, sd 0.35*sqrt(6)=0.857 → P(lead) ≈ 0.755. Eh. It's a modeling exercise; state assumptions.

Honest plan: implement analysis kind "match_lead_elo" in mathgen.py that takes: currentScore (each), gamesRemaining, eloGap, drawShareAssumption, and computes P(Sindarov strictly more points after N games) by enumeration (6 games → 3^6=729 outcomes — trivially enumerable exactly!). That's clean, exact computation given parameters, no simulation needed. P(yes) computed exactly. Assumptions: draw share (stated; default 0.7 with sensitivity 0.5-0.85 maybe), Elo from live fetch.

Given the small remaining context, I need to move to implementation NOW and be efficient. Architecture plan:

### Design

**Core: Source fetch layer (src/miners/live/sources.ts)**
- `fetchJson(url)` and `fetchHtmlText(url)` via direct fetch (Node fetch with UA header).
- `FetchedDoc = { url, kind: 'json'|'text', body: string|unknown, fetchedAt, httpOk }`.
- In mock mode: returned from LIVE_FIXTURES map (the verified live contents I just scraped, stored in a fixture file with fetchedAt=MOCK_NOW-ish).
- Everything flows through this layer — no numbers come from anywhere else.

**Per-topic refresher (src/miners/live/refreshers.ts)**
For each of the 10 topics + node one (maybe only the 10 with specs; node spec has no market in 30-70 band... skip node? Fix 1 says "Phase 1: live Path B fetcher + Python CSV calculators for wikipedia siteinfo, bun, go milestone, node dist, IETF". Implement refreshers for all 10 + node as spec (a "node-v26" spec could be registered for the Node market even though filter drops it — the calculator exists and is tested). Hmm, but specs without markets map to nothing. I'll implement a live calc function for node and test it directly (not in the pipeline), documented. Actually simpler: implement refreshers for the 10 spec'd topics; node gets a small standalone live calculator function + test. OK.

Each refresher: given fetched docs → produce `RefreshedSpec` = partial ResearchSpec fields (headline, figures, sourceDescriptions, links, analysis params with computed values, plus `facts` used for freshness + verification). Actually implement so that each figure string is *derived* from parsed live values — no hardcoding numbers in refreshers except URLs and market constants (threshold, market target like 7,275,500 = market param, fine).

**Freshness gating (fix 13)**: each market has a resolutionCriteria cutoff — parse the Market's evidenceCutoffAt? No wait: fix 13 says: "source fetch/publication timestamp must be AFTER each market's resolutionCriteria cutoff timestamp". Hmm — actually reading fixture markets: they have evidenceCutoffAt (when evidence submission closes). "resolutionCriteria cutoff" — reading FIX-LIST #13: "Freshness gate: source fetch/publication timestamp must be AFTER each market's resolutionCriteria cutoff timestamp (stale facts = $0)." Every market resolutionCriteria presumably states something like "evidence submitted after X counts"/"official figures" — I can't know the exact wording. Reasonable interpretation: sources must be fetched/published after some cutoff embedded in the resolutionCriteria string. Since resolutionCriteria text is real in the fixture, let me look at what it says. Then implement: gate compares each fetched source's publication timestamp (or fetchedAt) against the market's evidenceCutoffAt? No wait, that would make all sources stale (cutoff Nov 28 > publication Nov 18). Hmm, that can't be right either.

Let me read a fixture market's resolutionCriteria. Then design: the "asOf freshness" (fix 12) requires "asOf freshness check" — i.e., candidate.asOf/fetchedAt must be older than... Let me check resolutionCriteria text in fixtures-markets.json.

**Gate file-size/note-length check (fix 12)**: note ≤ 8000 chars; file size ≤ 10MB; domain check (links must be from prediction-market-allowed domains? no — "prediction-market domain check" means: our submitted links must NOT point to prediction/betting market sites (delphi.fyi links are banned content?). I think it bans citing prediction markets (e.g. delphi markets, Metaculus, Polymarket, bookmakers) as evidence sources. Implement DOMAIN_DENYLIST = delphi.fyi, manifold, polymarket, metaculus, kalshi, predictit, oddschecker, betting sites.
- phrase linter: ban judge-steering phrases ("please judge in favor", "you should rate this high", "award me", "judge this", etc.) + bookmaker URLs.

**Gate tests (fix for tests)**: item count (1 + links.length + files.length <= 3), slot counting (remainingOnMarket directly), note length, file size, freshness, domain check, phrase linter, lowercase addresses. 

**Fix 5**: items = 1 + candidate.links.length + 1 (the CSV file) —use actual links/files counts.

**Fix 6**: slots = entry.remainingOnMarket (server-tracked); do not subtract onlineSubmissionCount or log.submittedCount. Only subtract in-flight claims when batching — we do single drafts per market, so use directly.

**Fix 7 submitter hardening**: 
- refuse if manifest.submittedAt set
- inside submitDraft: re-run local checks: terms (client.getTerms), limits, entry-state, gate (need candidate reconstruction — simplest: verify by re-running gate-lite checks: item count from manifest, note length, file size, banned content, freshness vs asOf, market address format)
- log idempotency key BEFORE submitting to a sidecar file (append to evidence-log or a separate submit-attempt log; "log the idempotency key BEFORE submitting so a timeout retry reuses it")
- write back submissionId + idempotencyKey to ledger/manifest (update manifest.json submittedAt, submissionId, verdict fields)
- surface verdict/reason/bounty/zeroPayReason/settlementUpTo from waitForSubmission result — need SDK typings: let me check the SDK's submission data model.
- waitForSubmission timeoutMs: 30 * 60_000; stop when status rejected.
- CSV as File named "data.csv": new File([csv], "data.csv", {type:"text/csv"}) — Node 20 has File global.

**Fix 8**: CLI action `npm run accept-terms` → cli.ts "accept-terms" command — POST /v1/terms/acceptance via SDK client (does SDK have acceptTerms? check). Pipeline refuses as today, but with the pointer to run `npm run accept-terms`.

**Fix 9**: DE CPI: verify real Oct 2026 VPI from live fetch (126.5, +2.8%). verifySources extended: check note's pasted figures against scraped content (require at least 2 figures present in source text, or figures that contain numbers must appear — implement: every figure with a number token must have ≥1 of its numeric tokens present in the fetched source content; else warn/reject).

**Fix 10**: api-json/static-html live verification: fetch all links (not only scraped) in live mode; api-json parsed via JSON contains value; static-html: fetch directly (not via Firecrawl) and check expect needles.

**Fix 11**: mode-tag ledger entries: EvidenceLogEntry gets `mode: "mock"|"live"`; EvidenceLog constructor takes mode and ignores entries with other mode. Keep backward compat: existing entries without mode are treated as "mock" (so old mock entries don't block live). Ledger helpers (lockedStance, hasSignature, draftedCount, submittedCount) filter by mode.

**Fix 12/13/14**: as above.

**Fix 14**: Judge-proof attachments: the note already pastes figures; move "key figures at top". Compact CSV with URL + UTC timestamp columns. Update mathgen to append a "# source, fetched_at" header line into CSV. Also note structure: key figures right after headline.

**Fix 15**: move online-submissions check BEFORE mining: in pipeline, when processing each market, call listSubmissions before mining and pass to gate; we can keep it in the loop but before verifySources/analysis; better: fetch once per ranked market before mining. Actually "the online-submissions check (GET /v1/submissions?market=...) moved to BEFORE mining" — currently it happens after analysis (step 6 gate). Move it to right after the cap check and run the count through the gate context. Since the gate no longer needs onlineSubmissionCount (fix 6), we still want the check for... QA says "checked before mining" — the purpose: avoid wasting mining on markets where account already submitted 3 (or find duplicates). We'll do: before mining a market, listSubmissions(market) — if online count >= cap (3 or 1 restricted), skip with reason. Also record online submissions into log? Just the check.

**Fix 16**: draft.ts `${marketPct}%` → `${marketPct}`.

**Fix 17**: pipeline tap noSpec double-count: remove the loop-push (keep report init's list).

**Fix 18**: X_AGENT_ID default "siera-labs-evidence-miner".

**Fix 19**: evidence-log.ts: normalize marketAddress toLowerCase in comparisons (forMarket, and also in factSignature? The fix says comparisons — forMarket. I'll normalize in forMarket + lockedStance/hasSignature/draftedCount via a normalized address).

**Fix 20**: remove X-Delphi-Item-Budget header.

**Fix 21**: README docs for live smoke test: `npm run plan -- --mode=live` documented.

**Fix 2**: verified URLs in specs (as fallback seeds) + live fixtures for mock mode:
- DE: PD26_392_611.html (+2.8%, 126.5) + GENESIS 61111-0004 link (unreachable via static... GENESIS is a JS app — link as static-html would fail live verify. Better second link: Destatis theme page "Verbraucherpreisindex und Inflationsrate" _inhalt.html or the Nov 2025 press release PD25_447_611 (122,7). For the note, use PD26_392 + PD25_447 as the two links.
- CH turnout: stadt-zuerich stimmbeteiligung (39.6%) + gfsbern 2nd survey (Teilnahmeabsicht 52%)... plus ch.ch? two links fine.
- CH war materiel: gfsbern 2nd SRG survey (49/46) + srf article (2. SRG-Umfrage auf einen Blick) or admin.ch vote dossier. QA called it "SRG Wählbarometer" replacement: gfsbern news page = official SRG-commissioned. Second link: https://www.admin.ch/de/volksabstimmung-vom-29-november-2026 (vote dossier, 200 verified).
- ES Vox: electografica 261123 (19.1%, 64) + maybe the 261119 page for a second tracking point... or congreso.es apportionment (static-html; verify: congreso.es exists?). Let me keep 1-2 links: electografica + maybe "https://www.congreso.es/opendata/diputados-loi"... must verify 200. If not verified, use only electografica (links.length=1 fine).
- FIDE: fide.com/new-documents/ FACT SHEET (Match score 1-1, colors) + maybe the schedule news. 1-2 links.

**Fix 3**: Go milestone by title: live fetch milestones (paginated, search by title "Go1.27.5") → number 457, counts. Also go.dev/doc/devel/release — verify the minor listing format for parsing.

**Fix 4**: Wikipedia: live count 7,269,403; recompute required/day. Velocity: need 30d/90d history. Wikipedia statistics... the "Wikipedia:Size of Wikipedia" page or the article-count log. Let me check quickly whether any live source provides a history. Quick probe: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Size_of_Wikipedia (table of monthly counts?) or https://pagecounts... If nothing, compute velocity from... hmm. Zero-hallucination: velocity must be computed from live-fetched numbers. Maybe fetch the siteinfo twice? No. Alternative: https://commons... Let me probe "Wikipedia article count growth monthly" via search or fetch the page Wikipedia:Size of Wikipedia. Actually, a cleaner live source: "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Special:Statistics&useskin=vector" only current. Or the XTools? Let me do one probe: Wikipedia:Size_of_Wikipedia and "Wikipedia:Database reports/Pages by size"... I'll probe quickly.

Hmm wait — earlier QA itself said "counts only rise ~44/day" and "recompute the velocity math (required net 6,138 / 438 per day, not 4,266)". The velocity basis ([+43.7/day over 30d, +38.4/day over 90d]) came from wiki stats pages. Let me probe for a live source of monthly article counts. EN Wikipedia has "Wikipedia:Size of Wikipedia" with monthly milestone tables... may not be current. Alternative: stats.wikimedia.org — check availability: https://stats.wikimedia.org/#/en.wikipedia.org — JS. There's a REST: https://stats.wikimedia.org/htdocs/en.wikipedia/... hmm.

Practical fallback: the English Wikipedia maintains "Wikipedia:Version 1.0 Editorial Team/Assessment" no...

OK alternative: use the **siteinfo** current + the **PagePile**? Simpler: the API's "articlecounter"? Actually, there's https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&meta=siteinfo&siprop=statistics&format=json (current) and the "Wikipedia:Size of Wikipedia" monthly table. If the table page is not updated, we can still anchor velocity from TWO live endpoints: Wikimedia has "Article counts (monthly)" dataset at stats.wikimedia: https://stats.wikimedia.org/htdocs/dumps/... 

Let me just probe Wikipedia:Size of Wikipedia quickly. If thin, use "Wikipedia:Database reports"? Another idea: the "Special:Statistics" page shows a 30-day edit count but not article deltas.

Given effort limits: I'll do this — the Wikipedia live refresher fetches siteinfo and, for velocity, fetches the "Wikipedia:Size of Wikipedia" or fallback to the monthly-updated "Wikipedia:Version_1.0"? Let me probe the actual page now.
